purpose: One still of a character in one facing, edited from a reference image: the start frame of that facing's clips.
whenToUse: the facings a game draws (n, ne, e, se, s), each edited from the same approved master still
the master itself: a reference in the game's style redrawn at the isometric angle
a new character in an existing one's style: that one's master as the reference, the prompt replaces the subject
whenNotToUse: sw, w and nw: the game mirrors se, e and ne
the frames of a motion (the Flipbook video session animates the still)
art that needs transparency from this step: it keeps a plain background
gotchas: never run on a GPU: look at one render before a batch
the reference is the approved master, never another facing, so drift does not add up
one seed for every facing of a character
size and foot position can move between facings: compare them side by side on one ground line
no cutout: the plain background is what the video stage mattes
